inputs.text: ABU DHABI, February 17, 2026 (WAM) – The National Center for Meteorology (NCM) has issued a weather warning regarding potential fog formation and significantly reduced horizontal visibility across several western regions of the UAE. According to the NCM statement released on Tuesday, visibility is expected to deteriorate—and may drop to zero at times—starting from 21:30 tonight until 10:00 AM Wednesday, February 18. The Center has urged motorists to exercise extreme caution on the roads. Drivers are advised to follow all traffic safety guidelines, maintain a safe distance from other vehicles, and strictly adhere to modified speed limits, particularly in areas experiencing thick fog.

fields.description: Fog warning: visibility may drop to zero at times in western regions from 21:30 tonight (Tue 17 Feb) until 10:00 AM Wednesday 18 Feb. Source: National Center for Meteorology.
fields.headline: Fog warning: visibility may drop to zero in western regions tonight until 10:00 Wednesday
fields.instruction: Drive with extreme caution, keep a safe distance from other vehicles and follow modified speed limits in thick fog. More info: https://alerts.example.ae
fields.note_for_reviewer: I chose severity Moderate because the source calls the fog potential, but visibility near zero on roads could justify Severe. Please also confirm that the operator's demo Western zone matches NCM's 'several western regions', since the source does not name specific areas.

no_basis.concern: The bulletin gives no explicit severity or certainty grade, so Moderate and Likely are the drafter's judgement. The wording 'potential fog formation' and 'is expected to deteriorate' is consistent with them.
no_basis.searched_for: UAE or NCM clause defining CAP severity and certainty levels for fog warnings

NCM fog low visibility warning UAE early warning
alert must match meteorological bulletin times areas unverified reports
payload.summary: The alert matches the NCM bulletin: same hazard (fog / low visibility), same times (21:30 tonight until 10:00 Wednesday 18 Feb), same area (western regions), and the same precautions. It states that visibility may drop to zero at times, as the bulletin does. It includes no unverified report. Severity Moderate, urgency Expected and certainty Likely are plausible for a warning of potential fog and do not overstate or understate what the bulletin supports.

payload.summary: The sender is in the issuer register (level 1, all areas and categories). The alert area matches the area requested for event uae-fog-2026-02-17 (Western region demo zone, code AUH-WEST). The status Actual fits a real event on the live console. The msgType is Alert, so no references are needed. There are no active alerts from other authorities to overreach, and no earlier alerts to conflict with.

no_basis.concern: The phone text has no explicit protective action (e.g. drive carefully) on the first page. It gives the hazard, region and time only.
no_basis.searched_for: cell broadcast first page hazard and action

no_basis.concern: TDRA-TS040 summary says messages should be limited to 1 page maximum, whereas the alert runs to 2 (en) and 5 (ar) pages. It is a 'should' in a secondary summary, TS FS 001 v2.0 sets no page limit, and page length is a recorded gap (G6) with objection only above 15 pages.
no_basis.searched_for: TDRA cell broadcast handset specification page limit

queries: TDRA cell broadcast handset specification Arabic English
3GPP TS 23.041 cell broadcast page limit UCS-2
cell broadcast first page hazard and action
payload.summary: Both required languages (ar, en) are present. English is 2 pages and Arabic is 5 pages, both well under the 15-page cell broadcast maximum (3GPP TS 23.041: n equal to or less than 15). Encodings are appropriate (GSM-7 for English, UCS-2 for Arabic). Page counts are a recorded gap (G6), and I object to length only above 15 pages. The first page of each language opens with the hazard (fog warning, visibility dropping to zero), and the time window and region follow immediately. The text contains no explicit protective action. Whether an action is needed is a content question for other reviewers, and no clause shown to me requires one for delivery.

no_basis.concern: The Arabic was produced by machine translation and needs human review before release. No clause shown requires this in the UAE. The FCC texts that mention it are US material.
no_basis.searched_for: UAE or TDRA requirement for human review of machine-translated Arabic emergency alerts

no_basis.concern: Minor stylistic choices: the Arabic uses the masculine imperative (قُد) and the word 'أحيانًا' for 'at times'. Neither changes the meaning.
no_basis.searched_for: UAE Arabic wording or register guidance for fog warning instructions
